section.title: REVIEW OF PROPOSAL COMPONENTS
section.description: The proposal is separated into three sections.

question.text: • Section 2.1 characterizes the aquifer formation that each groundwater well in the West taps and

json.answer: compares well construction patterns before and after the establishment of regulatory controls.

section.title: • Section 2.2 estimates groundwater components of the water budget (withdrawals and consumption)

question.text: • Section 2.3 integrates research and education through the Scientist Spotlight and Hydrologic

json.answer: Sciences Workshops.

section.title: TYPES OF DATA
section.description: The PI and PhD student will be responsible for all data-related activities including: collection,

question.text: TYPES OF DATA

json.answer: documentation and metadata description, quality control, storage and backup, archiving, and sharing.

question.text: The project will result in new sets of data, code, and tools. These outputs include: (a) source code to

json.answer: quality control, collate, and merge datasets, (b) open source models and budgets in R and/or python, and

question.text: (c) sharable instructional materials (Scientist Spotlight activities and workshop materials).

section.title: Input data:
section.description: Available data will be systematically reviewed and downloaded. These data are likely

question.text: Input data:

json.answer: available in the form of Microsoft Access files or Microsoft Excel spreadsheets; shapefiles or raster files;

question.text: or text files or comma-delimited files. A multi-tier storage and quality assurance methodology will be

json.answer: adopted and will likely evolve as new datasets provide for challenging formats and organization.

section.title: Produced Data:
section.description: Datasets will be produced in Sections 2.1-2.3 of the proposal. These datasets will be

question.text: Produced Data:

json.answer: formatted and shared in an open format (e.g., CSV) or in illustrator files (i.e., cross sections).

section.title: DATA AND METADATA STANDARDS
section.description: The data will be shared along with a README.txt, which will describe all files, their relationships,

question.text: DATA AND METADATA STANDARDS

json.answer: naming conventions, etc. Data elements and attributes will be described following ISO 19115

question.text: specifications and metadata schema and standards in Hydrology (e.g., following any establish standards

json.answer: of the Water Information Coordination Program’s Open Water Data Initiative (Larsen et al., 2016)) to

question.text: allow for better interpretability and interoperability. Code and scripts produced in R and/or python will be

json.answer: documented for reproducibility purposes. The metadata for the codes will include: (1) description of the

question.text: functions required to operate the analyses; (2) description of input parameters and outputs; and (3) test

json.answer:
case, files and plots documenting the expected response of the model (Section 2.1) to a standard set of
input parameters. Documentation will focus on the description of the functions, input parameters, outputs,
the format of input data, instructions to run the model, and instructions to export the results. The outputs

question.text: will be stored in CSV format with a metadata document describing the data structure of the output data.

section.title: Raw data:
section.description: Detailed information about how the data were obtained, including detailed contact information

question.text: Raw data:

json.answer: or websites for direct download and citations to all datasets will be provided to allow for accessibility and

question.text: correct attribution to original collectors. All methodological procedures for data quality control and

json.answer: aggregation will be described in the data documentation. This information will be provided in the form of

question.text: supplementary documentation for publications, in the README.txt file, and at the repository (record-

json.answer:
level). All sharable raw data and the processed data will be archived in Dryad, https://datadryad.org, the
agnostic open access repository backed by UCSB and the California Digital Library (CDL), which
implements the latest best practices in data curation, publication, citation, and archival. Dryad assigns

question.text: Digital Object Identifiers (DOIs) to deposited datasets and makes data discoverable through such services

json.answer: as the Thomson-Reuters Data Citation Index, Scopus, and Google Dataset Search. All data in Dryad is

question.text: publicly accessible and released under a CC0 license. Data will be linked to publications and vice versa

json.answer: through DOIs.

section.title: POLICIES AND PROVISIONS FOR RE-USE, RE-DISTRIBUTION
section.description: All data deposited at Dryad will be publicly available under a CC0 license, meaning that others may

question.text: POLICIES AND PROVISIONS FOR RE-USE, RE-DISTRIBUTION

json.answer: freely build upon, enhance and reuse the works for any purposes without restriction under copyright or

question.text: database law. CC0 does not exempt those who reuse the data from following community norms for

json.answer: scholarly communication, i.e., reusing the data in a way that is mindful of its limitations and citing the

question.text: original data authors.

section.title: PLANS FOR ARCHIVING AND PRESERVATION OF ACCESS
section.description: UCSB Box will be used as the primary means to store and back up all collected input, generated output

question.text: PLANS FOR ARCHIVING AND PRESERVATION OF ACCESS

json.answer: data sets and code, and educational materials over the course of the project and prior to data sharing. Box

question.text: provides encryption of data at rest and in-transit, detailed logging of file actions, two-factor

json.answer: authentication, and access review of collaborators. Data will be accessed using Box Drive, which requires

question.text:
full disk encryption, firewall, and an antivirus software in order to install on a local computer.
At the end of the project, all shareable data accompanied by the appropriate documentation, metadata, and

json.answer: code will be deposited into Dryad for long-term storage, preservation and accessibility. Deposits

question.text: submitted to Dryad are curated prior to public release to conform with quality standards and enable future

json.answer:
reuse.
The source code for the research and education components (Sections 2.1, 2.2., and 2.3) will be saved,
stored, and backed up on the UCSB Box. A copy of the code will also be submitted with each of the three

question.text: planned publications. After the evaluation and refinement of the developed datasets and tools and once

json.answer: the research is completed and published, the final version of the tools and the documentation will be

question.text: shared on the UCSB’s Dryad Data Repository. The final shareable instructional and teaching materials

json.answer:
will also be shared via on a publicly accessible webpage (Scientist Spotlight) and UCSB Google Drive
(workshop materials) and Dryad in pdf format.
